title: 2007 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement:
A student at Harvard named Kevin

Was counting his stones by 11
He messed up \(n\) times
And instead counted 9s
And wound up at 2007.

How many values of \(n\) could make this limerick true?

solutions.text: 21. The mathematical content is that \(9 n+11 k=2007\), for some nonnegative integers \(n\) and \(k\). As \(2007=9 \cdot 223, k\) must be divisible by 9 . Using modulo 11 , we see that \(n\) is 3 more than a multiple of 11 . Thus, the possibilities are \(n=223,212,201, \ldots, 3\), which are 21 in number.
